display: Oud maker in Berlin: I build and repair Arabic and Turkish ouds in a courtyard workshop in Wedding. Winter is my slow season.

signals.text: Winter is my slow season, so I have room for new oud commissions and repairs.
I'm taking on one instrument for a Berlin festival and I'm happy to hear about other work that fits my workshop. I won't rush soundboards.
I'm in the middle of a twelve-string Istanbul-style oud. The soundboard bracing is the hardest part, and I'd enjoy talking it through with another maker or a player with a good ear.
My workshop is cold. The little stove struggles, and last January my glue froze solid. I need to insulate the north wall before the real cold arrives.
I'd like a spare pair of hands for a weekend of insulation work, and I'd like to do it for around 400 euros.
The price of gut strings has roughly doubled. I'm looking for a more stable supplier or other makers to share bulk orders with.
My German is B2 and still improving. I'd welcome patient conversation partners, especially for formal and official language.
I spend a lot of time helping family with German school and office paperwork, and I could use clear explanations of how those forms work.
I miss my home city sometimes, and on those days work is harder. I'd welcome company and conversation with people who know that feeling.
I'm going through the German naturalisation process and have an appointment coming up. I'd welcome encouragement and practical tips from people who have done it.
I'd like more players and friends to play backgammon and drink tea with on Sundays.
I can't plane or machine anything after 8pm because the neighbours complain, so evening-heavy plans don't suit my workshop.

offers.text: I build ouds to order: Arabic, Turkish and Persian (barbat), with hand-cut rosettes, bent ribs, bowl-back construction and soundboard bracing.
I repair ouds, including humidity cracks, seam opening, soundboard releveling and hide-glue work.
I carry three generations of oud-making knowledge and can teach or demonstrate rib bending and soundboard voicing, one-to-one or to a small group.
My workshop has a steam bender, rib moulds and hand planes. I could host a visit or a short hands-on session in Wedding, before 8pm.
I have a client list of about 150 players across Germany, the Netherlands and France. I can point makers or musicians to the right people.
I speak Arabic, German, English and some French, and I can help with oud-related communication across these languages.
I can offer advice on setting up and maintaining an oud, including choosing gut or nylon strings and keeping the instrument in Germany's dry-and-damp seasons.
Newly arrived families or newcomers can get my practical experience of rebuilding a working life in Berlin, from finding a workshop to getting started.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I play the oud in Hamburg and my instrument cracked in the dry heating season. Can someone repair it without damaging the original sound?
catchers.can: I can open the seam, relevel, glue with hide glue and refinish with shellac.
catchers.confirm: Is it a bent-rib oud or lute-family instrument with gut or nylon strings, and does it need no lacquer?

catchers.hypo: I'm a musician in Amsterdam and want a Turkish oud made to order for stage and recording. I'm happy to wait a few months for a good one.
catchers.can: I can take a commission and build it in the Istanbul style, with walnut ribs, a spruce top and a hand-cut rosette.
catchers.confirm: Are you after an acoustic oud with gut or nylon strings, and can you wait several months?

catchers.hypo: I run a world-music festival in Germany. Our guest player needs an oud fitted and checked on site before the concert.
catchers.can: I can do a fitting and set-up, and I can say honestly which jobs fit my schedule and workshop.
catchers.confirm: Is the instrument an acoustic oud, not electric, and is the work to be done before 8pm?

catchers.hypo: I'm a luthier making a lute or saz-family instrument. I'm stuck on bending ribs without cracking and I'd love a tip from someone who learned the traditional way.
catchers.can: I can explain how I steam, bend and mould ribs, and I may be able to invite you for a short session in my workshop.
catchers.confirm: Is your instrument built with bent ribs, as opposed to carved or laminated bodies?

catchers.hypo: I teach German in Berlin. A twelve-year-old at my school and his uncle are struggling with school forms and nobody explains them clearly.
catchers.can: My nephew's school and form questions are something I know well, and I can pass on how we managed the Anmeldung, or introduce a volunteer language teacher I trust.
catchers.confirm: Is this about helping a family with school or official forms in Berlin, not about legal immigration advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired teacher who volunteers with adult learners who want to improve their German for formal settings. Do you know people who would benefit?
catchers.can: I can introduce the volunteer teacher who has been helping me prepare, and I'll share what kind of practice works.
catchers.confirm: Are you offering free, one-to-one German practice for an adult who already speaks some German?

catchers.hypo: I'm from Aleppo and living in Berlin. I'm looking for a place to meet others from home, drink tea and play backgammon.
catchers.can: I can bring you to the Sunday backgammon table at a café with friends from Aleppo, or introduce a friend who knows the community.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for casual company in Berlin rather than any paperwork or political help?

catchers.hypo: I'm an oud student in Berlin and don't know which instrument to buy or how to look after it. Could someone explain what to look for?
catchers.can: I can talk through what a good oud sounds like and how to care for it, and I can suggest what to check before buying.
catchers.confirm: Are you a beginner or intermediate player who wants advice, not a lacquered or electric instrument?

catchers.hypo: I'm a carpenter or builder in Berlin with a free weekend. Do you need help insulating a cold workshop wall before winter?
catchers.can: I have a north wall to insulate before the real cold, and a budget of around 400 euros for materials.
catchers.confirm: Can you work on a single weekend job on a small courtyard workshop wall, with the work finished before 8pm?

catchers.hypo: I'm a gut and nylon string maker. I have stock and would like to sell to an oud maker who orders regularly.
catchers.can: I buy strings regularly for ouds and could be a repeat customer if the price is stable.
catchers.confirm: Do you supply gut and nylon strings suitable for ouds, not silk?

forbids.text: I only work on bent-rib lute bodies strung with gut or nylon.
I don't do lacquer work. I can refinish with shellac only.
I don't work on anything strung with silk.
I can't work after 8pm because the planer disturbs the neighbours.
I won't rush a soundboard to meet a deadline.

projects.name: Istanbul-style twelve-string oud
projects.text: A commissioned instrument in walnut and spruce with an ebony bridge and a hand-cut rosette, due before the end of the year. I'm open to a second pair of expert ears on the bracing.
roles_needed: oud player with a good ear
fellow luthier for a bracing opinion

projects.name: Winter workshop insulation
projects.text: Insulating the north wall of a cold courtyard workshop before the winter frost, as a weekend job.

policy.t1: When there's a real sign of a fit, I'll share what I make and what I refuse, my workshop schedule and my current commissions, and I can introduce people from my circle who suit the request.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and I know who you are, I'll share that I'm going through German naturalisation and that I sometimes feel homesick.
policy.never: I never share documents or papers, or family details from Syria.
